look_here_first: Dark-stemmed woody mimosa with strongly curved downward prickles, few pairs of pinnae, pale pink flower heads, and short red-brown pods.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: no more than about 7 leaflet pairs on longest pinnae

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: shorter red-brown pods, mostly sessile at base

lookalikes.differences: Compared with M. borealis, texana is darker, more zigzag, and more strongly hooked. Compared with M. biuncifera, it has fewer pinnae/leaflets and less strongly constricted pods.
